public_scope: Kim Question 5.5 for all finite hypergraphs with no Berge cycle whose length is divisible by three

source.paper: Jinha Kim, Topology of Independence Complexes and Cycle Structure of Hypergraphs

claim: If a finite hypergraph H has no Berge cycle whose length is divisible by three, then I(H) is contractible or homotopy equivalent to a sphere.
definitions: Berge cycle with distinct vertices and distinct hyperedges
source normalization by minimal nonfaces and removal of singleton edges

source_inputs.name: Kim hypergraph suspension theorem
source_inputs.role: shows the original connected nonisolated independence complex is a suspension

source_inputs.name: Kim edge-star expansion
source_inputs.role: iteratively suspends the independence complex while preserving absence of ternary Berge cycles

source_inputs.name: Kim ternary graph theorem
source_inputs.role: classifies the graphified independence complex as contractible or a sphere

source_inputs.name: Finite-CW topology
source_inputs.source: standard suspension homology, van Kampen, Hurewicz, and homology Whitehead
source_inputs.role: upgrades the integral homology dichotomy for a suspension to the homotopy dichotomy
